problem: On REVERIE, prior VLN agents represent navigable viewpoints with whole-image or object features. These are insufficient for concise high-level instructions, and the little training data makes it hard to align views with text and to explore efficiently in unseen environments.
motivation: REVERIE instructions such as 'bring me the blue cushion in the master bedroom' cannot be followed step by step, so the agent needs extra information inferable from what it sees. Humans use commonsense such as bed implies bedroom. Spatial and temporal links between concepts, such as hallway followed by living room, could generalize to unseen scenes.
key_idea: Build a CLIP-refined ConceptNet knowledge graph over detected objects and knowledge, add a concept-history node, encode the graph with graph-aware cross-modal attention, and add a commonsense-based local action-prediction branch to DUET.
insight: Commonsense knowledge helps only in moderation and only on tasks with concise instructions. The top-k ablation shows k=10 is best (SR 47.49), k=0 gives 46.72 and k=20 gives 47.25 because of noise. The module ablation shows small, gradual gains from KGS, concept history and the CD pipeline. The authors report no significant gain on R2R, whose fine-grained instructions make exploration and external knowledge less necessary.
method: Object detection: Faster R-CNN pretrained on Visual Genome yields all objects (1600 categories) in each navigable view.
Knowledge base construction: query ConceptNet with 8 selected relation types for each detected object, obtaining triplets such as (bed, AtLocation, bedroom).
Knowledge selection: CLIP-I/CLIP-T score each fact by average cosine similarity with the whole image and its objects, and keep the top-k (k=10).

Knowledge graph: object and knowledge labels are encoded by CLIP-T plus node-type and directional (heading/elevation) encodings. Nodes are connected by knowledge-base relations, plus an extra history node linked to all others.
History initialization: the [CLS] embedding of a BERT-style text encoder over the instruction initializes the concept history h0.

KG-aware cross-modal encoder: concepts and history act as queries in cross-attention over the instruction. Self-attention adds a learned bias from the adjacency matrix (M = A·Wa + b). The history is updated each step.
Concept aggregation: attention scores averaged over 12 heads and softmaxed give a weighted sum of concept tokens, yielding one concept feature per viewpoint.
Commonsense-based decision pipeline: a new branch produces a navigation score and an object score, fused with DUET's dynamic fusion and trained with an additional loss L_CD.

setting.backbone: DUET (topological map + global action planning, ViT-B/16 image features) with the ACK module, CLIP-T for concept encoding, BERT-style transformer (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: DUET pretrained on SAP, MLM, MRC and OG; ACK is only fine-tuned for 20k iterations on REVERIE, with ConceptNet as external knowledge
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with REVERIE-provided object boxes, plus detected object labels from Faster R-CNN
setting.action_space: discrete navigation-graph viewpoints (topological map) plus stop and object selection

numbers.extra: single-run; ACK only in fine-tuning stage

results: On REVERIE test-unseen ACK reaches SR 53.97, SPL 37.89 and RGS 32.77, beating the DUET baseline (SR 52.51, SPL 36.06) and KERM (SR 52.26). It improves every metric over DUET on both splits, but the gains are modest (about +1.5 SR). On val-unseen KERM/AZHP still have higher SR (49.02/48.31).
limitations: Gains over DUET are small (about 0.5 SR on val-unseen), and there was no significant improvement on R2R.
Depends on noisy ConceptNet retrieval and detector labels; too many facts (k=20) hurts.
Evaluated only on REVERIE in simulation, on top of the DUET architecture.
